subject: general
question: A shopkeeper offers a trade discount of 15% on the marked price of an item. If the marked price of this product is ₹6500, what is its selling price (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the discount is 15%, the Selling Price (SP) will be (100 − 15)% = 85% of the Marked Price.

SP = 85% of &inr;6500

SP = (85 ÷ 100) × 6500

SP = 85 × 65 = &inr;5525

**∴ The correct answer is &inr;5525.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = &inr;6500

Trade Discount = 15%

**Formula Used:**

Discount = (Discount % ÷ 100) × MP

Selling Price (SP) = MP − Discount

 MP: &inr;6500 
• 
 Discount: 15% −&inr;975 SP: &inr;5525 Selling Price = MP − Discount 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = (15 ÷ 100) × 6500

⇒ Discount = 15 × 65 = &inr;975

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 6500 − 975

⇒ SP = &inr;5525

**∴ The correct answer is &inr;5525.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on the label of an article. Any trade discount or promotional discount is always calculated strictly on the Marked Price.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the equivalent single discount can be calculated directly using the formula: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Profit and Loss Baseline

While discounts are calculated on Marked Price, the Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically mentioned otherwise.
